analysis:
The PR is a doc-only rewrite of docs/architecture/security/attestation.md. Only the base excerpt (lines 264-526) and the head excerpt (lines 1-261) were supplied, with no patch, so what was added or removed is inferred by comparison.

Relevant head claims:
- Lines 10-14 and 112 delegate authoritative authorization to the external darkbloom-platform repo. Receipt-required basic grants are superseded, missing receipt/risk evidence alone does not block basic serving, and an established identity may retain last-known policy within proof and administrative ceilings. This conflicts with the canonical header assertion that every serving grant needs a fresh verified risk receipt, and with T-053, T-057 and TB-011.
- Lines 48-76 describe provider connection control and the endpoint-resumption candidate. Dispatch is not blocked by model work; connection invalidation clears the old local grant. The custody response needs no Apple work, which is new attack surface for T-053 and T-054.
- Lines 25 and 29-37 cover qualification-generation recomputation and the ED-bit-less CDhash parsing, which only follows chain, ACL and nonce verification. This matches the existing model.
- Lines 80-104 cover the verification presentation and inventory registration-timestamp metadata. This is non-evidentiary, with no raw receipts exposed.

I found no concrete regression in the base lines 264-526 (the MDM, MDA, APNs and routing gate descriptions). The doc cites code that was not provided, so none of its claims were checked against source. The next pass should check whether the coordinator code actually enforces the platform semantics, and whether the revocation fence and the 30s snapshot ceiling hold under retained last-known policy.

findings.detail: The head text (lines 10-14, 112) says the external darkbloom-platform contract supersedes the retained coordinator snapshot. Basic serving is no longer blocked by missing recurring receipt/risk evidence. An established exact identity may retain last-known policy within the original ceilings, and receipt monitoring is split from `EvaluateAuthorization`. The canonical threat model still states that every serving grant needs a fresh verified risk receipt. It also relies on failed reads never extending authorization (T-053, T-057, TB-011, A-016). A provider with a revoked or risky credential, or one whose receipt/risk evidence is withheld or failing, could keep serving under last-known policy during admin-read or receipt outages until the ceilings expire. This is documented as the linked platform revision's behavior and not as deployed, so adoption is uncertain. The threat model needs updating to state the new freshness and ceiling assumptions and how revocation fences interact with retained policy. The docs should also say which repository enforces them, since the in-repo coordinator snapshot is now explicitly non-authoritative.
findings.title: Docs adopt platform semantics that drop the per-grant fresh risk receipt and allow last-known-policy retention; threat model still asserts the stricter rule

findings.detail: Head lines 69-76 describe an `app_attest_endpoint_resumption` candidate. `CoordinatorClient` answers it directly with the fixed process key and a socket nonce, without Apple work. A matching platform could then use that response together with retained evidence to resume or bind authorization to a new endpoint or connection. This differs from the previously documented requirement for a fresh current-endpoint assertion on every connection and endpoint binding. The threat model does not cover the new surface: a replayed or misbound custody response, a proof signed by the process key alone with no hardware-bound Apple freshness, a provider-side oracle that signs coordinator-supplied nonces, and deadline preservation. The threat model should add this path to TB-011, T-053 and T-054 and fix the required properties. The nonce must be single-use and bound to the connection and endpoint, original proof deadlines must not be extended, and revocation and qualification checks must be re-run at resume.
findings.title: New endpoint-resumption custody response is attack surface not covered by the threat model
